title: feat(revisions): let LAYA_REVISION pick the checkpoint commit
description:
## The gap

`laya/revisions.py` publishes `PINNED_REVISIONS` — the reviewed commit SHA of each shipped
checkpoint — and the package already has the plumbing that consumes a revision:
`resolve_revision` feeds the `revision=` kwarg of `snapshot_download`, which `Agent` records as
`agent.revision`, which `Router.loaded_revisions` publishes, which `/health` serves under
`revisions`. What was missing is the last inch: `resolve_revision` was a two-line function that
returned `revision or None`, so **nothing in `laya/` read the table**.

Counted over the package (probe, no weights, no network):

```
main                            0 line(s) naming PINNED_REVISIONS, besides its own definition
this branch                     4
```

So a deployment that wanted the reviewed commit had to pass a literal SHA at every call site —
while the *other* half of the same opt-in pair, in the same module, was already environment-shaped:
`expected_sha256` falls back to `LAYA_SHA256_DIGESTS`. This makes the pin reachable the same way,
so a container pins its checkpoints with one env line and no code:

```yaml
environment:
  LAYA_REVISION: reviewed        # or a commit SHA / branch / tag
```

## Measured

Same probe on both trees: `laya.load()` and `laya.Router` running for real against a tiny local
checkpoint fixture, with `huggingface_hub.snapshot_download` replaced by a recorder. Only the
transport is replaced — tokenizer, config parse, weight load and the revision bookkeeping are the
real ones. py3.14, CPU torch.

| load case | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no env, no argument | no `revision` kwarg | no `revision` kwarg (unchanged) |
| explicit `revision=` argument | that commit reaches the hub | that commit reaches the hub (unchanged) |
| `LAYA_REVISION=<commit>` | no `revision` kwarg | that commit reaches the hub |
| `LAYA_REVISION=reviewed`, bundle repo | no `revision` kwarg | `55cf4c4e…753851` |
| `LAYA_REVISION=reviewed`, standalone repo | no `revision` kwarg | `e4e9ddf2…f63a67` |
| `LAYA_REVISION=reviewed`, unkeyed repo | no `revision` kwarg | `ValueError`, **no download attempted** |
| `LAYA_REVISION=''` / `'   '` | no `revision` kwarg | no `revision` kwarg |
| local directory path, env set | no download | no download |
| `Router.loaded_revisions`, `reviewed` | `{'english': None}` | `{'english': '55cf4c4ebb4ebe31b2550e8bdf3bd21b99753851'}` |

Both loaders get it from one place: `agent.py:297` and `onnx_agent.py:102` both already called
`resolve_revision`, so the CLI, `examples/server.py`, the demo server, the MCP tools, the Docker
image and `laya-evals` all honour the variable without a change to any of them. Neither call site
is on the request path — `resolve_revision` runs at load, once per checkpoint — so there is no
per-request cost to measure.

## Design calls

- **Opt-in, not default.** Issue #332's closing constraint is that pinning must not become the
  default, because a pinned default breaks `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` loads from an older cached snapshot.
  Unset or blank returns `None`, i.e. exactly today's behaviour, and a test asserts that.
- **The caller's argument outranks the environment**, so an explicit `revision=` in code can never
  be overridden by ambient config.
- **`reviewed` resolves per repository.** The bundle and the two standalone repos have three
  different SHAs; one env line is then correct for whichever checkpoint a service loads.
- **`reviewed` for a repository the table has no entry for raises** instead of loading it unpinned.
  A pin that silently resolves to nothing is the failure mode this control exists to prevent, and
  `verify_digests` already refuses on the same principle. The error names the repository and the
  variable.
- **Blank is not a pin** (`""`, `"   "`, `"\t"`): an unsubstituted value in a compose template
  means "unset", not "download a ref called space".
- **`common.build_model` is excluded deliberately.** Its `AutoModel.from_pretrained` load is the
  training-time *base encoder* — a different repository, with no reviewed SHA in this table — and
  it takes `revision` as its own argument. A test asserts the env never reaches it, so the
  exclusion is a contract rather than an accident.

## Gate

10 new checks in `tests/test_download.py` (5 → 15 tests, 14 subtests), in the file whose subject
is already "what the download call was given", reusing its tiny fixture. They assert the revision
that reaches `snapshot_download`, the one the `Agent` reports back, and the one a real `Router`
publishes in `loaded_revisions` — i.e. the `/health` surface, not just the kwarg.

Why this file and not `tests/test_revision_pinning.py`, which is the content-wise closer home: this
one runs in both CI lanes (`ci.yml:107`, `release.yml:47`) while that one is in no workflow and has
three PRs queueing on it (#528, #568, #572). The reasoning is written into the file so the next
reader doesn't move it back into a suite that never runs.

Seven mutants, each caught by the named test whose clause it breaks (script: reset all files →
apply → run → restore from bytes read at start, tree asserted byte-identical after):

| mutant | named failures |
| --- | --- |
| resolver ignores the environment | `…environment_revision_reaches_the_download`, `…reviewed_resolves_each_repositorys_own_pin`, `…reviewed_refuses_a_repository_with_no_pin`, `…router_publishes_the_pinned_commit` |
| environment outranks the caller's argument | `…an_explicit_revision_outranks_the_environment` |
| no `strip()`, whitespace counts as a pin | `…an_empty_or_blank_environment_value_is_not_a_pin` |
| the sentinel literal drifts (`reviewed` passed to the hub as a ref) | `…reviewed_resolves_…`, `…reviewed_refuses_…`, `…router_publishes_…` |
| unkeyed repo quietly loads unpinned | `…reviewed_refuses_a_repository_with_no_pin` |
| the base-encoder exclusion is dropped | `…the_base_encoder_load_ignores_the_environment` |
| `Agent` stops reporting the revision it was given | `…environment_revision_reaches_…`, `…reviewed_resolves_…`, `…router_publishes_…` |

Whole-lane parity: every one of the 37 suites in the routing step runs in script form on this
branch with the same result as main — `test_revision_pinning.py` 20/20 (its
`resolve_revision(repo) is None` still holds with the env unset), `test_router.py` 546/0,
`test_hooks_api.py` 131/0 (nothing new in `laya.__all__`, so the contract line count is unchanged),
`test_load_errors.py` 17/0. Ruff (`E9,F63,F7,F82,F401,F811`, line-length 120) and
`python -m compileall -q laya/ tests/` clean.

## Overlap

- **#528** (keemsisi) documents this same table and its digest half in `docs/security.md`. It is
  docs-only and touches neither file here, so this PR is the code half of the same topic. Once it
  lands, `LAYA_REVISION` deserves a line there — I'd rather send that as a commit to his PR than
  edit his file from mine, and am happy to if he wants it.
- **#588** (mine) is the CLI form of the same control, `laya-evals run --revision`, for a one-off
  scoring run. Different surface, no shared file; the env form covers every load, including the
  evals runner's own.
- **#184** (devloper961-maker) asks that every model-free suite be wired into both lanes.
  `tests/test_download.py` is already in both, so this stays green whichever way that lands.
- Per-PR file lists (not title search): no open PR touches `laya/revisions.py` or
  `tests/test_download.py`.

bugs.summary: resolve_revision folds an explicit revision argument and LAYA_REVISION into one value, but the refusal for a reviewed pin the table lacks always blames the environment variable ("LAYA_REVISION=reviewed ... set LAYA_REVISION to a commit or unset it"), so a caller who passed revision="reviewed" through laya.load or Router is told to change a variable that is not set (or that holds a valid pin and is ignored), instead of the argument that caused the refusal.
bugs.trigger: Call resolve_revision("acme/custom-checkpoint", "reviewed") (or Router/load with revision="reviewed" for a repository missing from PINNED_REVISIONS), with LAYA_REVISION unset or set to a commit; the ValueError names LAYA_REVISION instead of the revision= argument.
